# Agent 1 — Bank Disclosures — Findings 2026-08-27

(Method: shared research harness — one agent per bank, adversarial per-claim verification, completeness gate, DETERMINISTIC table render. 42 bank(s) targeted, 42 returned signals, 616 verified signals. Confidence capped at Medium per single-agent playbook. Table rows ordered by Printec value (size x win), biddable first.)

## What changed since last run

The four biggest new items are all hard, verified fleet or mandate numbers. Hungary's statutory ATM build-out is now fully specified end-to-end — Act XVIII of 2025, the NGM rollout schedule (16/2025) and the MNB siting-and-cost-sharing rules (19/2025) — while OTP and MBH are both *shrinking* their Hungarian estates (OTP Core 1,987 to 1,929 ATMs in H1-2026), leaving a mandated installation gap someone must fill. Alpha Bank's Greek fleet is now a hard figure for the first time: 1,199 ATMs at 31/12/2025, of which 624 are off-site. BCR's locator census was independently reproduced (1,100 dispense-only ATMs plus 568 multifunctional), with 736 of the 1,100 carrying NCR asset IDs and 211 of 282 branches already tagged cashless. And PrivatBank's 2025 report plus Prozorro confirm both the scale (7,310 ATMs, 10,053 self-service terminals, 345,234 POS) and Printec Ukraine's own 39,000-terminal Castles award, alongside a competitive Diebold Nixdorf and Newland presence to defend against. Deposit-capability gaps are the run's dominant recurring pattern: cash-out-only shares of roughly 74% at UniCredit Bulbank, 80% at MBH, 66% at OTP Hungary, 70% at Erste Croatia, 60% at Stopanska, and zero deposit-capable machines across 1,094 independent-deployer ATMs in Croatia and all 144 Addiko Croatia machines.

Verification corrected or failed to confirm several baselines. The UniCredit Romania locator count (1,207 ATMs) and the Euronet-share reads for UniCredit and Raiffeisen Romania are contradicted; SLSP's "733 including 296 deposit ATMs" and Gorenjska banka's Slovenian fleet were both corrected; the NBG 1,476-ATM press figure is contradicted, with the Hellenic Bank Association's 1,360 at 31/12/2025 the reliable number; Romania's Law 239/2025 POS-acceptance mandate remains unconfirmed at primary source; and the Greek DIAS shared-ATM-operator story is still only partially confirmed and low confidence.

## Top opportunities (ranked)

1. **Hungary mandated ATM rollout (NGM/MNB, OTP, MBH, Erste)** — turnkey ATM supply, siting and managed services against the statutory installation schedule (XL, High).
2. **BCR Romania** — recycler/MFM upgrade of the 1,100 dispense-only ATMs plus in-branch cash automation for the 211 cashless branches (XL, High).
3. **PrivatBank Ukraine** — recycler refresh, TSO replacement and self-service managed services on a 7,310 ATM / 10,053 terminal estate where Printec already holds the POS hardware (XL, High).
4. **Alpha Bank Greece** — off-site ATM managed services and deposit automation across 624 off-site machines, ahead of the November 2026 Investor Day (XL, High).
5. **NLB Group (SEE)** — group-level ATM & CDS upgrade programme inside the EUR 160-200m technology envelope, plus merchant-acquiring POS against the >20,000-merchant target (XL, High).
6. **MBH Bank Hungary** — cash-in retrofit for the 1,029 cash-out-only ATMs, starting with the 803 legacy Takarékbank machines (XL, High).
7. **UniCredit Bulbank Bulgaria** — ATM obsolescence remediation named in its own 2026 risk outlook, targeting the 564 cash-out-only machines (XL, Medium).
8. **CEC Bank Romania** — deposit-capable MFM expansion behind Cash2Card and the Digital Agency format across a 2,511-site network (XL, Medium).

| National Bank of Serbia (regulatory clock on AikBank) | Serbia | PRIMARY TEXT RE-READ IN FULL (21-page official PDF). The NBS Decision on establishing and verifying the identity of a natural person by means of electronic communication ('video identification'), Executive Board no. 14 of 07/05/2026, published in Official Gazette RS 43/2026, sets these transitional rules. Point 36: enters into force on the eighth day after publication. Point 33: obligors already performing video identification under the 2019/2020/2021 decision must align their business and internal acts within SIX MONTHS of entry into force, and must adapt their TECHNICAL SOLUTIONS, where necessary, within ONE YEAR of entry into force. Point 35 repeals the 2019 decision (Sl. glasnik RS 15/2019, 84/2020, 49/2021) outright. Point 30: any obligor intending to offer video identification must notify NBS at least 30 DAYS before starting, submitting internal acts, proof of staff training, the list of document-issuing states its staff are trained on, proof of suitable premises, and a description plus prior assessment of the technical solution - and, in the same point (paragraph 5, NOT point 31 as originally cited), must give NBS staff a live, real-time DEMONSTRATION of the entire process for every category of customer before that 30-day period expires. Point 31 covers notification of any change of circumstances. The decision creates two modes: 'neposredna' (direct - a real-time call handled by an employee) and 'posredna' video identification (indirect), where the employee's supervision and verification can take place before the relationship is established or, exceptionally, within 72 hours afterwards under enhanced monitoring and transaction limits. | CEC Bank / all ATM operators in Romania | Romania | Senate bill B409/2026 has cleared all four advisory opinions with none opposing. The bill text (form transmitted to Parliament) inserts a new Art.221^1 into Law 209/2019 on payment services: payment service providers operating cash-withdrawal ATMs must let users key in a personalised withdrawal amount; this must be available to ALL users of cards issued by any PSP authorised to operate in Romania, regardless of card issuer; fast-cash preset buttons expressly cannot substitute for it; subject only to available cash, banknote mix and technical/security limits. Breach is a contraventie fined RON 50,000-100,000 where consumer interests are or may be affected, and operators get 90 days from entry into force to comply. Opinions on file: CES no.4693/14.07.2026 (favourable), Legislative Council no.679/22.07.2026 (favourable), National Bank of Romania no.G/161/17.08.2026 signed by Governor Mugur Isarescu, and Competition Council no.RG 11539/18.08.2026 signed by President Bogdan M. Chiritoiu. BNR says the measure 'ar putea contribui la cresterea accesului la numerar, in special in mediul rural' and concludes 'sub rezerva celor mentionate anterior, BNR nu se opune' (subject to the reservations above, BNR does not oppose), asking that the text (a) clarify whether the terminal-reconfiguration obligation also binds PSPs authorised in other Member States operating in Romania under Art.56 of Law 209/2019, (b) resolve that the text covers all 'utilizatori' while the sanction regime is framed only around consumers, with no rules for legal-entity beneficiaries, and (c) be consulted with the banking system 'in vederea identificarii aspectelor care vizeaza bariere potentiale in implementarea uniforma a caracteristicilor tehnice ale terminalelor de plata'. The Competition Council finds nothing contrary to Law 21/1996 or national/EU State-aid rules. The initiator requested urgent procedure on 24/06/2026; the last recorded Senate action is the 18/08/2026 Competition Council opinion - no committee report or vote is on file at 27/08/2026. | [Senate of Romania - legislative file B409/2026, with the bill text (26b409FG.PDF), explanatory memorandum (26b409EM.PDF), BNR opinion (26b409BNR.PDF) and Competition Council opinion (26b409CC.PDF)](https://www.senat.ro/legis/lista.aspx?nr_cls=b409&an_cls=2026) | 18/08/2026 | The last procedural obstacle that could have killed this bill is gone - the central bank explicitly declined to oppose it. Every ATM in Romania, including CEC's ~1,500 ATMs/MFMs, would need an application/screen-flow change and re-certification inside 90 days, which almost no bank can do in-house. That is a market-wide, deadline-driven ATM software and managed-services engagement. Better still, BNR has formally invited consultation with the banking system on the technical characteristics of terminals - an open door for a vendor with a ready compliance answer to shape the spec before the text is fixed. Note the explanatory memorandum frames the problem as the on-us/off-us interface difference, i.e. exactly the multi-acquirer screen-flow layer Printec sells. | Medium-High - all advisory opinions in and none opposing, but still first-chamber with no committee report and no vote scheduled | Medium | M | Medium | Track the Senate committee report and vote.
